payload.name: Preserve prior facts during memory updates
payload.description: When updating or merging an existing memory, use before replacing content: keep previously stored facts unless the new message explicitly contradicts them, and store distinct new events separately.
content: During UPDATE or MERGE, preserve all previously stored facts in the target memory unless the new message explicitly contradicts or supersedes them; never replace the existing content with an unrelated new event.

When a new message describes a distinct event, activity, or state rather than additional details about the existing memory, do not reuse that memory slot; ADD a new memory or update the memory that matches the new evidence.

Before changing object_text, world_start, or replacing content, verify the new evidence describes the same event; if it does not, leave the existing memory unchanged and store the new fact separately.

solves: This solves memory overwrite failures where an UPDATE replaces an existing memory's content with a different, unrelated event, causing previously stored durable facts to disappear from the final snapshot. The abstract failure mechanism is conflating new information about the same memory with a new distinct event. The rule to preserve prior facts unless explicitly contradicted and to store distinct events separately transfers across any multi-event conversation and prevents durable facts from being lost during later enrichment.
